prompt: What does the section call perhaps the best method of aldehyde synthesis?

choices.text: Oxidation of a primary alcohol with the Dess–Martin periodinane
Oxidation of a secondary alcohol with the Dess–Martin periodinane
choices.why: Oxidizing a secondary alcohol gives a ketone, not an aldehyde.

choices.text: Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene with an acid chloride
choices.why: Friedel–Crafts acylation gives aryl ketones such as acetophenone.

choices.text: Hydration of an alkyne with HgSO4 and H3O+
choices.why: Mercury-catalyzed hydration of an alkyne gives a ketone, as in the conversion of 3-hexyne into 3-hexanone.

explanation: Perhaps the best method of aldehyde synthesis is oxidation of a primary alcohol, usually with the Dess–Martin periodinane in dichloromethane at room temperature. Geraniol, for example, gives geranial in 84% yield.

prompt: The partial reduction of an ester to an aldehyde with diisobutylaluminum hydride (DIBAH) is normally carried out at what temperature, in °C?
explanation: The DIBAH reduction is normally run at −78 °C (dry-ice temperature) in toluene solution. Methyl dodecanoate, for example, gives dodecanal in 88% yield.

prompt: Methyl dodecanoate, CH3(CH2)10CO2CH3, is treated with DIBAH in toluene at −78 °C and then with H3O+. What is the product?

choices.why: Complete reduction of the ester would give this alcohol. DIBAH at −78 °C gives the partial reduction product, the aldehyde.
DIBAH is a reducing agent. Turning the ester into the acid would be hydrolysis, not reduction.

choices.text: No reaction; DIBAH doesn't react with esters
choices.why: Partial reduction of esters is exactly what DIBAH is used for in aldehyde synthesis.

explanation: Certain carboxylic acid derivatives can be partially reduced to aldehydes. The partial reduction of an ester by DIBAH in toluene at −78 °C is an important laboratory-scale method; methyl dodecanoate gives dodecanal in 88% yield.

prompt: How would you prepare pentanal from 1-hexene, CH3CH2CH2CH2CH=CH2?

choices.text: 1. BH3, then H2O2, NaOH; 2. Dess–Martin periodinane
choices.why: Hydroboration–oxidation keeps all six carbons, giving 1-hexanol and then hexanal, not pentanal.
DIBAH partially reduces esters. 1-Hexene has no ester group.
The Dess–Martin periodinane oxidizes alcohols. 1-Hexene has no –OH group.

explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves the C=C bond. 1-Hexene loses its terminal CH2 carbon as formaldehyde, leaving the five-carbon aldehyde pentanal (Exercise 19.2.1).

prompt: How would you prepare pentanal from 1-pentene, CH3CH2CH2CH=CH2?

choices.text: 1. BH3, then H2O2, NaOH; 2. Dess–Martin periodinane

choices.why: Ozonolysis cuts off the terminal CH2 carbon, giving the four-carbon aldehyde butanal plus formaldehyde.
Acid-catalyzed hydration follows Markovnikov's rule and gives 2-pentanol, which oxidizes to the ketone 2-pentanone.
Hydroboration–oxidation does give 1-pentanol, but NaBH4 is a reducing agent. An oxidant such as the Dess–Martin periodinane is needed to reach the aldehyde.

explanation: Hydroboration–oxidation adds water with non-Markovnikov regiochemistry, giving the primary alcohol 1-pentanol. Oxidizing it with the Dess–Martin periodinane then gives pentanal, with all five carbons kept (Exercise 19.2.1).

prompt: Which alkene gives a ketone (acetone) when treated with O3 and then Zn?

choices.why: Each alkene carbon has only one alkyl group, so ozonolysis gives two molecules of the aldehyde acetaldehyde.
Neither alkene carbon is disubstituted, so ozonolysis gives aldehydes: propanal and formaldehyde.
Ethylene gives only formaldehyde, an aldehyde.

explanation: Ketones can be made by ozonolysis of alkenes in which one of the unsaturated carbon atoms is disubstituted (Section 8.8). In 2-methylpropene, (CH3)2C=CH2, the disubstituted carbon becomes acetone and the =CH2 carbon becomes formaldehyde.

prompt: What product forms when benzene reacts with acetyl chloride, CH3COCl, in the presence of AlCl3?

choices.why: Benzophenone has two phenyl groups. Acetyl chloride brings an acetyl group, so the carbonyl carbon carries one phenyl and one methyl.
Acylation attaches the whole acetyl group, –COCH3, not a formyl group.
Friedel–Crafts acylation leaves the carbonyl group in place, so the product is a ketone, not an alkylbenzene.

explanation: Friedel–Crafts acylation of an aromatic ring with an acid chloride and AlCl3 catalyst (Section 16.3) gives an aryl ketone. Benzene and acetyl chloride give acetophenone in 95% yield.

prompt: Hexanoyl chloride, CH3CH2CH2CH2CH2COCl, reacts with lithium dimethylcopper, (CH3)2CuLi, in ether. What is the product?

choices.why: The methyl group replaces the –Cl on the carbonyl carbon, so the carbonyl ends up at carbon 2 of the seven-carbon chain.
Hexanal would need a hydrogen in place of the chlorine. A diorganocopper reagent transfers an organic group, here a methyl.
The acid would need an –OH group in place of the chlorine. The copper reagent supplies a methyl group instead.

explanation: Ketones can be prepared from acid chlorides and lithium diorganocopper reagents (Section 10.7). The methyl group replaces the chlorine: hexanoyl chloride and (CH3)2CuLi give 2-heptanone in 81% yield.

choices.why: The Dess–Martin periodinane oxidizes alcohols. 3-Hexyne has no –OH group.
DIBAH partially reduces esters to aldehydes. 3-Hexyne has no ester group.
Lindlar hydrogenation reduces the alkyne to cis-3-hexene; it doesn't introduce a carbonyl group.

explanation: Mercury(II)-catalyzed hydration of an alkyne gives a ketone (Section 9.4). 3-Hexyne is symmetrical, so water can add either way and gives only 3-hexanone (Exercise 19.2.2).

prompt: Bromobenzene is converted into acetophenone by: 1. Mg; 2. CH3CHO; 3. H3O+; 4. CrO3. What compound does CrO3 oxidize in the last step?

choices.why: The Grignard reagent C6H5MgBr adds to acetaldehyde, so the alcohol carbon carries both the phenyl group and a methyl group.
The phenyl group bonds to the carbonyl carbon of acetaldehyde, which becomes the carbon bearing the –OH.
Acetophenone is the product of the CrO3 oxidation, not the compound being oxidized.

explanation: Magnesium turns bromobenzene into the Grignard reagent C6H5MgBr. Addition to acetaldehyde, then H3O+, gives the secondary alcohol 1-phenylethanol, and CrO3 oxidizes this secondary alcohol to the ketone acetophenone (Exercise 19.2.2).
